About this page

  • In this page we review the literature which document the development of Adela’s cfMeDIP-seq Technology. The source of all the information contained therein is public. The primary references are the following:1

Variability in cfMeDIP-seq Data

  • The key components of the assay - filler DNA and antibody instance - are associated with a considerable amount of variability.
    • docname provides a detailed look at the Methylated DNA Immunoprecipitation Stage of the protocol.
    • questions to address:
      • how does the filler DNA operate? where does the variability come from?
      • how does anti-5-methylcytosine (5mC) antibody work? where does the variablity come from?
      • can variability be attributed to its proper source - anti-5-methylcytosine (5mC) antibody or filler DNA?
  • Rerun the analyses which assess the performance of the spike-in controls.

4 DNA Methylation-Based Cancer Diagnostics: Company Landscape

Regulatory status as of early 2026. LDT = laboratory-developed test (CLIA-certified lab, not FDA-cleared).

4.1 Company Table

Company / Product Use Case Sample Cancers Methylation Approach Regulatory / Stage Geography
GRAIL / Galleri® Multi-cancer early detection screening Blood Multi (>50) cfDNA targeted methylation sequencing (>100K CpG loci); tissue-of-origin ML classifier (CCGA study) LDT commercial; FDA Breakthrough Designation US, EU (NHS pilot)
Exact Sciences / CancerGuard™ Multi-cancer early detection + CRC Blood Multi Methylation + somatic mutation + protein biomarker combination; leverages CancerSEEK platform from Johns Hopkins; ASCEND-2 study (n=11,000) Clinical validation US (Abbott acquisition pending)
Guardant Health / Shield MCD Multi-cancer early detection Blood Multi (bladder, CRC, lung, pancreatic) cfDNA methylation analysis; NGS-based; tissue-of-origin prediction LDT commercial; FDA Breakthrough Designation US
BillionToOne / Northstar Response® Treatment response monitoring (stage III–IV) Blood Pan-cancer Tumor-naive methylation; QCT™ single-molecule counting of >2,200 cancer-specific methylated loci; absolute tumor burden quantification LDT commercial US (Nasdaq: BLLN)
Burning Rock Biotech / OverC™ / ELSA-seq Multi-cancer early detection + MRD Blood Multi (9–22 cancers) Deep methylation sequencing of cfDNA (ELSA-seq); 161,984 CpG sites; ML tissue-of-origin; THUNDER study (n=2,385) CE mark; FDA Breakthrough Designation China, EU, US (Nasdaq: BNR)
Singlera Genomics / PanSeer™ Multi-cancer early detection Blood Multi (CRC, esophageal, liver, lung, stomach) Methylation haplotype analysis; 12,000 methylation sites across 600 regions; contiguous CpG pattern phasing on single molecules Clinical validation US, China
Nucleix / Bladder EpiCheck® Bladder cancer surveillance & detection Urine Bladder qPCR methylation across 15 genomic regions in urinary cells; objective 0–100 score; sensitivity 91% high-grade, NPV 99% FDA 510(k) cleared; CE mark US, EU
Epigenomics AG / Epi proColon® 2.0 / Epi proLung® / HCCBloodTest CRC screening; lung & HCC detection Blood CRC, lung, HCC PCR methylation of SEPT9 (CRC), SHOX2 (lung), SEPT7 (HCC); plasma cfDNA; first FDA-approved blood-based CRC test (SEPT9) FDA approved; CE mark; currently restructuring / asset sale pending US, EU, China
MDxHealth / AssureMDx™ Bladder cancer diagnosis Urine Bladder qPCR combining FGFR3/TERT/HRAS mutation status + methylation of OTX1, ONECUT2, TWIST1 in exfoliated urinary cells; sensitivity 97%, specificity 83% LDT commercial US, EU
Adela / Adela MCED Multi-cancer early detection Blood Multi cfDNA methylation-based analysis with ML; fragmentation pattern integration Development US, Canada
Precision Epigenomics / EpiSeek™ Multi-cancer early detection screening Blood Multi (>12 types) Methylation-specific PCR; proprietary software-derived marker panel; distributed via TruDiagnostic (~40K clinicians) LDT commercial US
EarlyDiagnostics / CancerRadar™ Multi-cancer early detection Blood Multi cfDNA methylation + ML algorithms; blood-based multi-analyte signal detection Development US
Genomictree / EarlyTect® Bladder / Colon Bladder & CRC detection Urine / Blood Bladder, CRC qPCR methylation of multiple genomic/epigenomic targets in cfDNA from urine; East Asian validation studies Approved (Korea) Korea, East Asia

4.2 Key Observations

4.2.1 Technical differentiation

Companies split into roughly three technical tiers:

  1. Genome-wide or large-panel cfDNA methylation sequencing — GRAIL, Burning Rock, Singlera. These interrogate tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands of CpG sites and rely heavily on ML classifiers for both cancer detection and tissue-of-origin prediction. Highest information content but also highest cost and analytical complexity.

  2. Targeted qPCR methylation of specific validated loci — Nucleix, Epigenomics, MDxHealth, Genomictree. These anchor on a small number of well-validated methylation markers (e.g., SEPT9, SHOX2, OTX1) and use PCR-based quantification. More commercially mature, lower cost, and further along in regulatory clearance — but inherently single-cancer or narrow-scope.

  3. Hybrid multi-analyte approaches — Exact Sciences (CancerGuard), Guardant (Shield). These combine methylation signals with somatic mutation profiles and/or protein biomarkers to boost sensitivity, particularly for early-stage cancers where cfDNA shedding is low.

BillionToOne sits in a distinct niche: their QCT™ technology turns methylation into a precise quantitative tumor burden metric (absolute molecule counting) rather than a binary detection signal, making it better suited for longitudinal treatment monitoring than early detection screening.

4.2.2 Commercial maturity spectrum

Nucleix (Bladder EpiCheck) and Epigenomics AG (Epi proColon) are the oldest players with actual regulatory clearances. However, Epigenomics AG is now in financial restructuring (asset sale to New Day Diagnostics pending as of 2024). The urine-based bladder cancer niche (Nucleix, MDxHealth, Genomictree) is more commercially mature than the blood-based MCED space, because the signal-to-noise problem is more tractable in urine for a single organ.

Among blood-based MCED players, GRAIL’s Galleri is the furthest along commercially (LDT, NHS pilot, Pathfinder 2 study n=35,000). Guardant’s Shield MCD and BillionToOne’s Northstar Response are commercially launched as LDTs. Most others remain in clinical validation or development.

4.2.3 Geographic split

Several methylation-based MCED tests have advanced further in Asia before entering US/EU markets:

  • Burning Rock (OverC / ELSA-seq): CE mark obtained 2022; extensive China-based validation studies (THUNDER, PREDICT, PRESCIENT); FDA Breakthrough Designation obtained subsequently.
  • Singlera Genomics (PanSeer): large retrospective validation conducted in collaboration with Fudan University; detection up to 4 years pre-clinical diagnosis demonstrated.
  • Genomictree (EarlyTect): approved in Korea; validation studies primarily in East Asian cohorts.

This geographic pattern reflects both the high GI cancer burden in East Asia (making CRC, liver, and esophageal cancers natural targets) and more accessible early-stage regulatory and study infrastructure in China and Korea.

4.2.4 The Adela distinction

Adela (formerly known as Grail’s spinout focus for non-blood approaches) uses a cfDNA methylation approach that also incorporates fragmentation patterns — recognizing that nucleosome positioning leaves interpretable marks on cfDNA fragment lengths in addition to the methylation signal itself. This multi-modal epigenetic signal may improve sensitivity at low tumor fractions.

Table compiled from public sources. Last updated: March 2026.
